clue.text: Go to other bank in quest of note

parts.note: to go for something is to go in quest of it
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: A traveller heads to another bank looking for a banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money, which 'note' seems to support; here it is a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: To ford a river is to wade across to the opposite bank at a shallow crossing.

clue.text: Glance right, taking in strange choice

indicators.note: one piece takes the other in, holding it inside itself
strange letters are oddly arranged, so this word is reshuffled

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to look rightwards while weighing a peculiar decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glance' reads as a quick look, but here it is the verb for a strike skimming off a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A glance is a strike that skims off at an angle, as a bullet does when it rebounds.

clue.text: Look repeatedly said to create maximum annoyance

indicators.note: said points to words spoken aloud, and repeatedly because two clue words each sound like the entry

parts.note: a peak is the maximum or highest point

explanation.surface: Saying the same thing over and over is the best way to annoy someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple clue: 'annoyance' is PIQUE, which, like PEAK for 'maximum', is spoken exactly as the entry, hence 'repeatedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To peek is to take a quick or furtive look at something.

clue.text: Initially places in a post, perhaps

definitions.text: Initially places in a post, perhaps

parts.words: Initially places in a post, perhaps
parts.note: reads as an instruction about first letters, but simply describes putting someone into a job for the first time

explanation.definitionFit: To appoint someone is to place them in a position or office, such as a post on a committee.

clue.text: Labour leader will soon get rid of duplications

indicators.note: each doubled letter in the two words is cut back to a single one, so the repeats go

explanation.surface: A prediction that the Labour Party head will soon stop repeating himself.
explanation.walkthrough: WILL SOON has a double L and a double O; dropping one of each leaves the name. Harold Wilson led the British Labour Party and was Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Wilson was leader of the UK Labour Party in the 1960s and 1970s.

clue.text: Monarch frantically restricting rise of evil, such as 23? So some claim

indicators.note: the shuffled word hems in the other piece, confining it
something done frantically is wildly disordered, so this word is rearranged
in a down clue a rise means reading upwards, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: sin is wickedness or evil

explanation.surface: A frenzied king holds back the tide of wickedness, like a legendary ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend places King Arthur's birth at Tintagel in Cornwall, the south-western tip of England, hence 'So some claim'.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur is said in legend to have been born at Tintagel, which would make him a native of Cornwall.

clue.text: Clean house no more

parts.note: over means finished, no more

explanation.surface: Someone declares they will never clean the house again.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is US presidents: Herbert Hoover was one, though the clue does not need it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoover is the British verb for cleaning with a vacuum cleaner, from the brand name.

clue.text: Spot in Hautes-Pyrénées

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the French place name

explanation.surface: Spotted somewhere in a mountainous region of south-west France.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, which is one sense of spot as a verb.

clue.text: This girl's in love, as it happens

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O
a live broadcast shows events as they happen

explanation.surface: A young woman reveals that she has, as it turns out, fallen in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in love' looks like romance; 'love' is the tennis nil.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a girl's given name, so 'this girl' is a name.

clue.text: Deadly pious, soon converted

indicators.note: converted letters are changed into a new form, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sinister remark about devout people who will soon undergo a religious change.
explanation.definitionFit: Something poisonous is toxic and can kill, which is what deadly means.

clue.text: Handles books don ordered about queen

indicators.note: the reshuffled words go round the other letter, encircling it
the words are put in a new order, which signals rearrangement

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A university teacher arranges his books in some fashion around the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handles' looks like a verb; it is a plural noun. 'don' is a university teacher in the surface, plain letters in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Door knobs are the round handles by which doors are opened.

clue.text: One labouring to produce second volume in blue

indicators.note: one letter goes inside the colour word

parts.note: navy is a dark shade of blue
V is the abbreviation for volume, here a second one added to the V already present

explanation.surface: A worker produces another book in a sad or blue mood.
explanation.walkthrough: NAVY already holds one V; 'second volume' adds another.
explanation.definitionFit: A navvy is a manual labourer, especially one digging roads, canals or railways.

clue.text: Saint's working as self-proclaimed harmless drudge

parts.note: St John is a saint; with the possessive the name gains an S
on means operating or working

explanation.surface: A saint's toil described as that of a humble, inoffensive labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson's Dictionary defined a lexicographer as 'a harmless drudge', so the phrase points to the compiler himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson, who compiled the famous 1755 English Dictionary, called a lexicographer a harmless drudge, describing himself.

clue.text: Clothing for Frenchmen or Englishwomen

definitions.meaning: denim trousers are an item of clothing
Jean is a man's name in France but a woman's name in England, so the plural names either group

explanation.definitionFit: Jeans are denim trousers, and the plural of the name Jean fits French men and English women alike.

clue.text: Hit I have in a regular series

parts.note: a hit is a success, like a hit record
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a hit in a run of regular programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Successive things follow one another in an uninterrupted order, as in a regular sequence.

clue.text: Opening for an inspiring act

parts.note: sounds like a warm-up show before an uplifting performance, but inspiring here is breathing in through an aperture of the face

explanation.definitionFit: A nostril is one of the two openings of the nose through which air is drawn in.

clue.text: Brand name that gets blanket coverage

parts.note: a product line is a brand range

explanation.surface: A brand name whose advertising reaches absolutely everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blanket coverage' suggests saturation advertising; it is bed sheets lying under a blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: Bed linen, the sheets on a bed, is what a blanket covers.

clue.text: Like part of Greece that's reachable by several flights

definitions.meaning: Attica is the region around Athens, and its adjective describes things from there
a room at the top of a house is reached by climbing many flights of stairs

explanation.definitionFit: Attic describes Attica in Greece, and an attic is the top-floor room up several flights of stairs.

clue.text: 13 across, in short, from South America

parts.note: AM is a short form of America, as in AmE for American English

explanation.surface: A short reference to someone hailing from South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 across is the lexicographer Samuel Johnson, whose first name shortens to the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sam is the short form of Samuel, the first name of the lexicographer Johnson.

clue.text: Reproduce, in many respects, with pronounced difference

definitions.meaning: living things reproduce by increasing in number
the adverb formed from multiple, meaning in many ways, ends in a 'plee' sound

explanation.walkthrough: The verb is said 'multi-ply' and the adverb 'multip-lee': same spelling, 'pronounced difference'.
explanation.definitionFit: To multiply is to breed and increase in number; as an adverb the same letters mean in multiple ways.

clue.text: Wine servant passed around company

indicators.note: the first word goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a man is a manservant

explanation.surface: A servant circulates the wine among the company of guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passed around' suggests serving drinks to guests, which fits the wine, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mâcon is a French wine from the Mâconnais area of southern Burgundy.

clue.text: European raincoat in fashion

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means to shape anew, so the word is remade into a new order

explanation.surface: A continental who wears a stylish raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Croatian is a native of Croatia, a country in Europe.

clue.text: Mix drink when eating fish

indicators.note: the drink takes the fish inside it, as if consuming it

parts.note: to sup is to drink by sips
hake is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An instruction to mix a cocktail while dining on seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix drink' looks like a cocktail order; 'Mix' alone is the definition, as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A shake-up is a thorough reorganisation or mixing around, as of staff.

clue.text: A king dreadfully hurt, finally

indicators.note: this piece comes last, after the article and the royal letter

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: dreadfully means badly, signalling that the word's letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A monarch, at the end, badly wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes King Arthur, mortally wounded at the battle of Camlann at the end of his reign.
explanation.definitionFit: Legendary King Arthur received a fatal wound in his last battle, against Mordred.

clue.text: Break through, taking rook with knight, say

indicators.note: the chess piece takes in the other letter, holding it

parts.note: a knight is an example of a chess piece
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess move: capturing a rook with a knight to break the defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' sounds like a chess capture; here it puts R inside PIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to make a hole by forcing a way through something.

clue.text: Left officer in pub in city

indicators.note: the officer goes inside the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer

explanation.surface: An officer was abandoned in a pub somewhere in town.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln is a cathedral city in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln is an English cathedral city, the county town of Lincolnshire.

clue.text: Nobody can remember what it tastes like!

definitions.text: Nobody can remember what it tastes like!

parts.words: Nobody can remember what it tastes like!
parts.note: seems a complaint about bland food, but recalls the Homeric fruit whose eaters forgot everything

explanation.definitionFit: In the Odyssey, those who ate the lotus fruit lost all memory and desire to return home.

clue.text: A number of Germans practised deception

definitions.meaning: a number is a song, and a German art song is called by this word

explanation.definitionFit: A lied is a German song, a musical number; lied is also the past tense of lie, to deceive.

clue.text: Altered one's state with drug before awfully grim date

indicators.note: the drug letter comes first, ahead of the rearranged words

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone changed their state of mind with drugs before a terrible date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altered one's state' looks like intoxication, which 'drug' backs up; it means moving country.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's country to live in another, changing the state one lives in.

clue.text: A number of Indians in newspaper article

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Several Indian people featured in a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number of Indians' suggests a headcount; it is a piece of Indian music.
explanation.definitionFit: A raga is a melodic form in Indian classical music, so it is a musical number of India.

clue.text: Turned up only a little information

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading from the bottom, so the phrase is reversed

parts.note: a tad is a little

explanation.surface: Research turned up only a scrap of information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' sounds like found; it reverses A TAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures collected as information.

clue.text: Questionable European who, in France, gets singing part

parts.note: qui is French for who
the vocal is the sung part of a piece of music

explanation.surface: A dubious European from France is given a singing role.
explanation.definitionFit: Something equivocal is ambiguous and open to doubt, hence questionable.

clue.text: Admit king and queen, perhaps

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
a queen is an example of an ant, the egg-laying female of a colony

explanation.surface: Royal couple's acknowledgement, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'king and queen' looks like a royal pair; the queen is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant a point is to concede or admit that it is true.
